findings: Whole DedupeEngine.java reviewed: URL normalization or name-similarity buckets of reading source records; representative selected by metadata score and original order. No byte/perceptual content observation in this file.

Representative score rewards preferred name keywords, enabled flag, filled fields, rule completeness, short names and recency. Such preference is product ranking, not evidence files are interchangeable.

NAME mode inserts groups into one map by normalized first name and ungrouped entries by URL. Potential namespace collision needs NameSimilarity/model contracts and runtime before calling data loss; not reproduced.

Whole NameSimilarity.java read: grouping compares every candidate only to first unused anchor, marks matches used, then quality-sorts group. This is neither connected components nor all-pairs equality; nontransitive similarity can yield order-dependent groups. Static source conclusion, Java runtime not executed.

Similarity is Levenshtein normalized by maximum UTF-16 length plus common-prefix and substring bonuses, capped1; normalized strings<=4 require exact equality. This is name heuristic, not image/file equality.

Two ranking implementations differ: DedupeEngine adds short-name bonus5/3 while NameSimilarity.score omits it despite comment claiming consistency. Group pre-sort and final re-sort can select different representatives; actual fixture not run.

normalize delegates NameCleaner first; its local code does not lowercase final result even though comment says lowercase. Whether upstream cleaner supplies case folding remains unreviewed; no demonstrated case bug claimed.

Whole NameCleaner confirms no case folding; normalize therefore retains English case despite documentation. Cleaner removes zero-width controls and broad emoji/symbol ranges and collapses selected Unicode whitespace. Static source observation, no Java execution.

Complete/standard URL keys preserve nonempty fragment identity labels; requestUrl drops fragment for transport only. Aggressive key intentionally drops scheme/path/query/fragment and www prefix, retaining nondefault port. Thus same-host grouping intentionally does not establish resource/content identity.

Standard query strips configured tracking parameter names after URL-decoding names, sorts retained raw parts, and trims one trailing path slash. Complete key does not sort query. No HTTP requests or content comparisons performed.
